question: At an 85th-percentile approach speed of 45 mph, from how far in advance should the two primary signal faces be continuously visible, and what treatment is recommended if that view is unavailable?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The two primary signal faces should be continuously visible from at least the minimum sight distance in Table 4D-2 in advance of the stop line; however, the evidence provided only lists Table 4D-2 values up through 35 mph (325 feet), so the specific distance for a 45 mph approach speed cannot be quoted from this evidence. If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for that minimum distance, the recommended treatment is to install a warning sign (per Section 2C.35) alerting drivers to the signal. Additionally, at 45 mph or higher, backplates and specific signal face arrangements are recommended. Guidance (recommended): - "The two primary signal faces required as a minimum for each approach should be continuously visible to traffic approaching the traffic control signal, from a point at least the minimum sight distance provided in Table 4D-2 in advance of and measured to the stop line," unless precluded by a physical obstruction or another signalized location is within this range. (Note: the excerpted Table 4D-2 shows distances only for 20–35 mph, ending at 35 mph = 325 feet; the 45 mph value is not included in the evidence provided.) - "If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for at least the minimum sight distance shown in Table 4D-2, a sign (see Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the traffic control signal." - "If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on an approach to a signalized location is 45 mph or higher, signal backplates should be used on all of the signal faces that face the approach." - On approaches with 85th-percentile speeds of 45 mph or higher, new or reconstructed installations should follow Section 4D.05: primary signal faces per Table 4D-1, overhead faces approximately over the center of each through lane (when equal in number to through lanes), overhead faces over mandatory turn lanes, all primary faces on the far side of the intersection, consideration of supplemental faces for visibility behind large vehicles, and backplates on all signal faces. Citations: - Section 4D.06 Guidance §5 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §6 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §17 (p.671) - Section 4D.05 Guidance §7 (p.668) Note on sufficiency: The exact minimum sight distance for a 45 mph approach speed is governed by Table 4D-2, but the table excerpt in the provided evidence stops at 35 mph, so the precise 45 mph figure cannot be stated from this evidence.
gold_answer: They should be continuously visible from at least 460 feet in advance of the stop line. If at least two faces are not continuously visible for that distance, a warning sign should be installed for approaching traffic.
